evals.prompt: Write an ECLiPSe program with library(ic) that solves a 4x4 magic square (entries 1..16, every row, column and diagonal sums to 34) and prints the rows.
evals.expected_output: A runnable model file that prints one valid square
assertions: Loads library(ic) with a directive and gives every cell a domain with ::
Resolves the alldifferent ambiguity with :- import alldifferent/1 from ic_global if ic_global is loaded
Labels the cells with labeling/1 or search/6 and runs with eclipse.exe -f model.ecl -e main

evals.prompt: In ECLiPSe, count all solutions of the 8-queens problem and print the first one.
assertions: Labels the queens inside the goal handed to findall/3
Uses #\= constraints for rows and diagonals
Prints 92 as the count

evals.prompt: Solve a 0/1 knapsack in ECLiPSe: weights 12, 7, 11, 8, 9, values 24, 13, 23, 15, 16, capacity 26. Maximise the value.
assertions: Uses bb_min/3 from library(branch_and_bound) on a negated value held in a variable
Posts Cost #= -Expr first, since bb_min needs a variable as cost
Prints 51

evals.prompt: Pick 3 of 5 people with costs 3, 1, 4, 1, 3 in ECLiPSe for the cheapest team, and list every team with that cost.
assertions: Finds the optimum with bb_min/3
Enumerates all optimal teams with bb_options{solutions:all} or by fixing the cost and using findall/3
Reports 2 teams

evals.prompt: Schedule a 3-job, 3-machine job shop in ECLiPSe and minimise the makespan.
evals.expected_output: A makespan with start times per task
assertions: Loads ic_edge_finder for disjunctive/2 or cumulative/4
Posts one no-overlap constraint per machine and job precedences with #=<
Minimises with bb_min/3 on a variable bound to the max of the end times

evals.prompt: Find the shortest tour through 6 cities in ECLiPSe given a distance matrix.
evals.expected_output: Tour length with the visiting order
assertions: Uses circuit/1 on successor variables
Reads arc lengths with element/3 (1-based)
Loads lib(listut) if it uses nth1/3

evals.prompt: Write an ECLiPSe program that reads a JSON file path from the command line, reads a cost matrix, assigns workers to tasks at minimum total cost and prints one JSON line.
evals.expected_output: A model reading JSON with lib(json) and printing one JSON line
assertions: Takes the path from argv(all, L) (second element)
Parses with json_read/3 and names_as_atoms
Prints with json_write/3 and indent(0)
